From: Maya Thompson <security@bridgepoint.com>
To: rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 20 May 2025 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: BridgePoint RFP: Application Security questionnaire and deliverables

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for taking this RFP. As part of our procurement review we need a set of technical deliverables to validate Redwood's vulnerability lifecycle and runtime posture. Please provide the following artifacts and clarifications by end of next week (27 May):

1) SAST and DAST coverage: tooling used, scan cadence, false-positive handling and remediation SLAs.
2) Patch SLAs: timelines for critical/important/medium vulnerabilities from discovery/patch availability to deployment.
3) Recent third-party penetration test summary (redacted is fine) and remediation status.
4) SBOM for the primary inference runtime and key OSS dependencies.
5) Any SOC2/Security attestations or shared audit reports.

We will accept secure file sharing links (Drive/SharePoint) or attachments. If there are any questions about scope, please let me know today so we can raise internally.

Regards,
Maya Thompson
Security Lead, BridgePoint Financial

Rachel / team,

Quick update on SAST/DAST and patch SLAs:

- SAST: We run an internal SAST (Semgrep for infra + CodeQL for core services) on every PR; weekly full repo scans via CodeQL. False positives are triaged by the owning team within 48 hours; security-engineering supports classification. Attachments: last-sast-summary-202504.pdf (internal).
- DAST: Dynamic scans of staging endpoints using OWASP ZAP on a nightly job for public-facing services and weekly for internal APIs where feasible. Critical findings create tickets in Jira and are routed with P1 labeling.
- Patch SLAs (matrix attached): critical (CVSS >=9) — 72 hours from vendor patch availability or exploit confirmation; high 7-8.9 — 7 days; medium 4-6.9 — 30 days. Note: deployment SLA assumes automated deployment pipeline healthy; emergency hotfixes can be escalated to on-call. See patch-sla-matrix.xlsx (attached).

I can pull the last three SAST/DAST executive summaries and provide a sanitized summary for external sharing by EOD Friday.

-Karthik
Lead, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list and the timeline. Attached are the artifacts we can share without an NDA; where full reports are sensitive we included redacted summaries and a path to request the original under a standard NDA. Summary of what's enclosed: 

1) SBOM_BridgePoint_20250520.csv — bill-of-materials for the primary inference runtime (generated from our SBOM pipeline; license flags highlighted).
2) pen-test-summary-redacted.pdf — executive summary of the most recent third-party test (scoping, severity breakdown, remediation status). Redactions applied to exploit PoC details. Full report available under NDA.
3) patch-sla-matrix.xlsx — our standard patching/mitigation SLAs and escalation flow.
4) SAST/DAST executive summary (text below) and links to sanitized reports in Drive.

SAST/DAST executive summary:
- SAST: Combination of CodeQL and Semgrep covers ~95% of critical code paths for the inference runtime and orchestration services. Weekly full scans; false-positive triage within 48 hours.
- DAST: OWASP ZAP scans run nightly for external endpoints and weekly for internal testbeds. Findings are triaged in Jira; critical issues trigger emergency response and hotfix releases.

We have also uploaded a secure folder with the sanitized artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cBridgePointEvidence. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/89765 (recorded delivery).

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute walk-through of the artifacts and remediation posture early next week.

Regards,
Rachel Kim
Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference
